title: U Cinn - NEFA Concentration
author: Patrick Tso
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xmnfk5e
materials: Prepare working Color Reagent Solutions A and B. A. Reconstitute Color Reagent A with a portion of Solvent A and then transfer entire contents into Solvent A bottle, rinsing Color Reagent vial several times. B. Reconstitute Color Reagent B with a portion of Solvent B and then transfer entire contents into Solvent B bottle, rinsing Color Reagent vial several times.

steps.title: Prepare Standards and Samples
steps.instruction: Locate the working Standard (1mmol/L or 1 mEq/L). Note that this assay does not require a serial dilution.

steps.title: Load Plate
steps.instruction: Pipette 5μL of deionized water, 1mM standard, or sample to be assayed into separate wells of a 96 well flat bottom plate.

steps.title: Perform First Incubation
steps.instruction: Add 200μL of Color Reagent Solution A to all wells, mix well, and incubate the plate for 5 minutes at 37°C.

substeps.instruction: Add 200μL of Color Reagent Solution A to all wells

steps.title: Measure Initial Absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of each well at 550nm (sub:660nm) to obtain the sample blank value (Abs1).

steps.title: Perform Second Incubation
steps.instruction: Add 100μL of Color Reagent Solution B to all wells, mix well, and incubate the plate for 5 minutes at 37°C.

substeps.instruction: Add 100μL of Color Reagent Solution B to all wells

steps.title: Measure Final Absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of each well at 550nm (sub:660nm) to obtain the Abs2 value.

steps.title: Calculate Final Absorbance
steps.instruction: Calculate the final sample absorbance by subtracting the corrected first reading from the second reading.

steps.title: Determine Sample Concentration
steps.instruction: Construct a calibration curve by plotting absorbance vs. concentration using a linear calculation model, or use the calculation formula.

substeps.instruction: Use formula: Sample Conc. = (Sample Absorbance/Standard Absorbance) * Standard Concentration
